stories.headline: TENNESSEE COMPLETES SUFFRAGE VICTORY; MOVE TO RECONSIDER IS FEARED TODAY; PARTIES SPUR BATTLE FOR WOMEN'S VOTES; AMENDMENT WINS, 50 TO 46 "Antis" May Attempt to Force Fight for Rescinding it.TWO DAYS LEFT FOR ACTIONOpponents Prepare to AttackRatification on Constitutional Grounds.CONVERTED BY HIS MOTHERLegislator Whose Vote Turnedthe Scale Is Lionized bythe Suffragists.
stories.summary: The Tennessee legislature voted to ratify the amendment granting equal suffrage to American women, making Tennessee the 36th state to approve it, as suffragists celebrated the milestone, during the women's suffrage movement in the United States. The vote was a significant step towards securing women's right to vote.

stories.headline: RAILWAYS GET $1,500,000,000 MORE IN RATES; 40 PER CENT. FREUGHT INCREASE IN EAST; ALL PASSENGER FARES TO GO UP 20 PER CENT.; ROADS TO EARN 6 PER CENT. Investment Is Fixed by the Commission at $18,900,000,000. WESTERN ROADS DIVIDED "Mountain Pacific Group" Is Formed--South Gets 25% Increase and West 35%.SURCHARGE ON PULLMANSThis Goes to the Roads--MilkWill Pay 20% More, as WillExcess Baggage.
stories.summary: The Interstate Commerce Commission granted railroads a significant rate increase, allowing them to earn more revenue, as the rail industry sought to recover from financial difficulties, during a time of economic change in the United States. The increase would affect freight and passenger fares.

stories.headline: REDS FLEE BEFORE POLES, ABANDON GUNS; 30,000 CUT OFF, BREST-LITOVSK CAPTURED; SOVIET PLEDGES POLISH INDEPENDENCE; SIX RED DIVISIONS TRAPPED Capture of 30,000 to 40,000 Prisoners Expected on East Front.SEVEN DIVISIONS CRUSHEDPilsudski Moving Troops to CutOff Russians' Main Lineof Retreat.BUDENNY HELD AT LEMBERG Soviet Cavalry Leader Only 9 Miles from That City--Polish Peasants Fight with Scythes.
stories.summary: Polish forces defeated the Soviet Red Army, capturing key cities and territory, as the Polish-Soviet War intensified, with Polish leader Pilsudski playing a crucial role in the conflict. The Soviet troops were in full retreat, abandoning guns and equipment.

stories.headline: REDS IN DESPERATE RALLY TO SAVE ARMY; POLES, WARNED BY WILSON, WON'T INVADE; PREMIERS BAR DEMAND TO DISARM POLAND; TRAPS ARE CLOSED ON REDS Northwest Troops Must Cut Through, Yield, or Flee Into Prussia. ESTIMATE 75,000 PRISONERS Bialystok Taken as Two Armies Under Haller and Pilsudski Strike Russian Centre. LEMBERG SAVED FROM FOE Budenny's Cavalry Retreats Toward Southeast--7,000 Reds Interned in Prussia.
stories.summary: Despite a desperate rally, the Soviet Red Army was trapped by Polish forces, with many troops expected to be captured or forced to flee, as President Woodrow Wilson warned against invading Soviet territory, during a time of international tension. The Polish army, led by Pilsudski, was making significant gains.

rounds.blurb: Tennessee's legislature ratified the amendment granting equal suffrage to American women. The vote made Tennessee the 36th state to approve it, securing a significant step towards women's right to vote. Polish forces defeated the Soviet Red Army, capturing key cities and territory.

stories.headline: ARMED LINER SUNK BY THE BRITISH; Cruiser High Flyer Sends Kaiser Wilhelm der Grosse to Bottom Off African Coast. WAS COMMERCE DESTROYER British Lose One Killed and Five Wouded ;- Survivors of Kaiser Landed. GERMAN CRUISER SMASHED Magdeburg, Stranded and Attacked by Russians, Blown Up ;- 17 Killed ;- Mines Sink Two Ships.
stories.summary: The British cruiser High Flyer sank the German liner Kaiser Wilhelm der Grosse off the African coast, resulting in casualties and survivors being landed, as the war at sea intensified during the early days of World War I

stories.headline: KAISER IGNORES JAPAN'S DEMAND; TIME LIMIT ENDS; German Government Makes No Reply to Ultimatum ;- War Is Probably Now On. ENVOY ORDERED TO LEAVE Japanese Charge Instructed Throug h Washington to Quit Berlin at 4 A.M. Today. JAPAN EMBARKS TROOPS Shanghai Hears That 16,000 Men Are on Transports Ready to Move on Kiao-Chau. BIG FLEET ALSO ON PATROL London and Washington Both Believe Japan Will Begin Attack on Germans at Once. ALL NON-COMBATANTS FLEE American Ambassadors to Take Charge of Japanese and German Interests in Hostile Lands. KAISER IGNORES JAPAN'S DEMAND
stories.summary: Japan's ultimatum to Germany expired without a response, likely triggering war, and Japan began mobilizing troops and fleets, while ambassadors prepared to take charge of interests in hostile lands, amidst the escalating global conflict

stories.headline: Kaiser at the Front With His Three Sons; Berlin Press Hails His Act With Enthusiasm
stories.summary: Kaiser Wilhelm arrived at the front with his three sons, a move hailed by the Berlin press, as the war effort gained momentum

stories.headline: ITALY WITH 800,000 MAY JOIN THE ALLIES; Swiss Papers Learn of Country-Wide Preparations for War ;- French Frontier Vacated.
stories.summary: Italy, with a large military force, considered joining the Allies, with its attitude influenced by England's stance, as the complex web of alliances shifted during the early stages of the war

rounds.blurb: The sinking of the German liner Kaiser Wilhelm der Grosse by the British cruiser High Flyer occurred off the African coast. Germany's disregard for Japan's ultimatum likely triggered war with Japan. Kaiser Wilhelm arrived at the front with his sons amidst escalating conflict.

stories.headline: SCHOOL PLAN SET BY NEGRO PARLEY; Association to Petition Local Boards in South to Act at Once to End Segregation School Plan Set by Negro Parley; Fast Action at Local Level Sought
stories.summary: A Negro association plans to petition local school boards in the South to end segregation immediately, seeking fast action at the local level during the Civil Rights era. The group aims to dismantle segregated schools.

stories.headline: PARIS SENDS HEAD OF ARMY TO STUDY INDO-CHINA CRISIS; General Ely's Report Will Be Basis for New Talks With Washington on Help U. S. SCANS INTERVENTION Top-Level Officials Reweigh Possibilities in Light of Latest Developments French Generals Going to Indo-China PARIS SENDS HEAD OF FORCES TO ASIA
stories.summary: As the situation in Indo-China worsens, French General Ely is sent to assess the crisis and report back to Paris, which will be the basis for new talks with the US on a revised aid program, with Secretary Dulles conferring with President Eisenhower. The US is considering intervention.

stories.headline: SERVICE TAX DIES; 5% ADMISSION LEVY INDICATED FOR CITY; Auto Use Impost Due to Stay -- Estimate Board Bars Water Rate Rise RESERVE FUNDS RETAINED Board Rejects State Proposal for Use of Realty and Tax Appropriation Moneys BOARD OF ESTIMATE KILLS SERVICE TAX
stories.summary: The New York City Board of Estimate rejects a proposed service tax, opting instead to maintain an auto use impost and retain reserve funds, after considering a state proposal on reserve funds. The board also bars a water rate rise.

stories.headline: MONITORED CALLS STIR NEW DISPUTE IN M'CARTHY CASE; Democrats Would Reveal All or None -- Republicans Try to Limit the Disclosures GILLETTE WARNS SENATE Says on the Floor That Panel Has Violated Men's Rights and Chamber Must Act Army's Monitored Phone Call Stir Dispute in McCarthy Case
stories.summary: A dispute arises in the McCarthy case over monitored phone calls, with Democrats pushing for full disclosure and Republicans trying to limit the revelations, prompting Senator Gillette to warn that the panel has violated individuals' rights. Senator Symington urges complete disclosure.

rounds.blurb: The French government sent General Ely to Indo-China to assess the worsening crisis. The US considered intervention as Secretary Dulles conferred with President Eisenhower. A Negro association petitioned local school boards in the South to end segregation immediately.
